runs.text: 1 John 1:9
If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Jesus holds many titles including, Messiah, Savior, Son of God, son of man, and friend of sinners. In Hebrews 2:17, Jesus is identified as our High Priest. (See also Hebrews 4:14)

The office of priest was instituted at Mount Sinai when God gave the law to the Israelites. Out of the many priests, one was selected as the high priest who would enter the Holy of Holies once a year on the Day of Atonement. The high priest entered the Most Holy Place once a year to perform a ritual that removed the sins of the people from the sanctuary.

The opening text of this study (1 John 1:9) explains several things: it tells us that not only does Jesus’ blood pay the penalty for our sins, but that He also cleanses us from all unrighteousness. This cleansing is not what atones for our sins. The blood of Christ alone pays the price for our sins. (See tract 2, “
Justified by Faith Alone
”) This cleansing is a deep examination of the sin that lies latent within our hearts.

We have sinful natures because of the brokenness that happened to mankind when Adam and Eve ate the forbidden fruit. When they ate this fruit, Adam and Eve’s descendants had a change in their nature. Instead of outward love toward others, their nature then became bent inward towards self. This depravity lies deep within all of humanity and requires a high priest to root it out. As a rule, man cannot see the true nature of sin in his own heart.

It is for this reason that Christ became our High Priest. Christ alone understands the feelings of our infirmities. “He knew what was in man.” (See John 2:25, Hebrews 4:15) He was fully tempted as we are yet without sin, and He knows exactly how to succor (assist) us. This work is His High Priestly ministry. He took upon His sinless nature our fallen nature so that He could understand us and gently bring us to see the depth of our sin. As He shows us our sin, we can then confess and repent of our sin and have it placed in the heavenly sanctuary to be blotted out of our sub-conscience at the end of time. The final generation of fallen man will then be able to stand before God and be washed with pure water and be cleansed. This final cleansing is a cleansing of our conscience. Without this cleansing, sin would remain latent in our sub-conscience mind only to possibly resurface later in heaven, bringing the heavenly courts back into rebellion.
GOD PRUNES THOSE CONNECTED TO THE VINE:
1. How much fruit have those who abideth in the vine?
John 15:5
I am the vine, ye are the branches:
He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit
: for without me ye can do nothing.
Note:
The Father is the root, Christ is the vine, we are the branches. The fruit is God’s fruit. He is the source of the vine. We can only bear fruit when we are connected to God through Christ.
2. What does this fruit look like?
Galatians 5:22
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
Meekness, temperance.
Note:
The fruit is of the Spirit. It is God’s fruit. We obtain it from Him when we crucify (mortify) our flesh and walk in the Spirit. (See Galatians 5:24, Romans 8:13)
Galatians 5:24 And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.
3. How does God help those who bear fruit?
John 15:2
Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and
every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.
Note:
To purge means that He “prunes” (NIV) those who bear fruit so they will bear more fruit.
4. What does God do to those who do NOT bear fruit?
John 15:2
Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away
Note:
God does not prune those who do not bear fruit, He "takes away" those who do not bear fruit.
5. Does the Bible really say that He takes away those who do not bear fruit?
John 15:2
Every branch in me that beareth not fruit
he taketh away.
Note:
To “taketh away” does not seem to fit God’s love and His plan of salvation! But if we dig a little deeper, we find in Strong’s Bible Concordance the following definition of "takes away”!
142 To raise up, elevate, lift up.
1a) to raise from the ground, take up: stones.
1b) to raise upwards, elevate, lift up: the hand.
1c) to draw up: a fish.
After inserting “lifts up” in the place of “takes away”, we see that God does love us! He is the positive force in our life. He lifts up those who bear no fruit!
6. How does God clean the new branches?
John 15:3
Now
ye are clean through the word
which I have spoken unto you.
Note:

New grape branches tend to hang low near the ground. They get muddy when it rains which prevents the branches from getting oxygen. They also get no nourishing sunshine. So He washes them! Verse 3 says, He cleanses us with His word. He lifts us up so we get more oxygen and more nourishing sunshine.
7 Who did Jesus say would be thrown into the fire?
Matthew 3:7, 10
But when he saw many of the
Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire.
(See also Matt 7:19)
Note:

If we do not have fruit, i.e., we are young, or carnal, He doesn't cast us off. No! He loves us, He lifts us up and feeds us. He feeds us with His word. But the Pharisees, Sadducees, and false prophets saw no need to be cleansed by Jesus. They had no repentance. They are hewn down and cast into the fire. But those who see their need of cleansing, God will in no wise cast out. (See John 6:37)
8. What does chastening yield in our lives?
Hebrews 12:11
Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
Note:

Once we have the experience of abiding and bearing small fruit He prunes us. Thus, pruning yields the peaceable fruit of righteousness. Knowing that God increases His fruit of righteousness by pruning us brings peace during troubled times.
CLEANSING OF OUR CONSCIENCE:
9. What is cleansed at the end of days?
Daniel 8:14
And he said unto me, Unto two thousand and three hundred days;
then shall the sanctuary be cleansed.
Note:
When this time prophecy is calculated we learn that there is a final cleansing that takes place in the end days.
10. Where is this sanctuary located?
Hebrews 8:1
Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest,
who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens
A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
(See also Exodus 25:9, Hebrews 9:24)
Note:

This cleansing is the cleansing of the “true tabernacle” located in heaven. The second sanctuary was the tabernacle in Israel. The first (true) tabernacle is located next to the throne of God in heaven.

For us to understand this verse we have to first understand how the tabernacle in Israel operated. The heavenly tabernacle is part of the ultimate disposition of all sin, typified by the cleansing of the ancient Hebrew sanctuary each year on the Day of Atonement. The heavenly things are purified with the perfect sacrifice of the blood of Jesus. The heavenly cleansing at the end of days will last for all eternity.
11. What is purged in the true tabernacle?
Hebrews 9:14
How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God,
purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God
Note:

In Israel, they took the blood of the sacrifice and sprinkled some of it on the mercy seat in the earthly tabernacle. By faith this transferred the sins from the offender to the Most Holy Place of the tabernacle. Then once a year on the Day of Atonement the sanctuary was cleansed.

At the end of time we by faith take our sins to Christ our High Priest, and then in the final cleansing on the antitypical day of atonement, He will cleanse our conscience from our sins. (See Hebrews 9:14)

If we were to just stop committing the acts of sin we would still have the underlying reason for the sin in our sub-conscience. Then when we arrive in heaven, the reason for the sin would still exist in our character, and the rebellion could resurface. Christ still has work to accomplish in us. (See Hebrews 2:17, 3:1)
12. Who is the High priest that makes reconciliation for the people?
Hebrews 2:17
Wherefore in all things
it behoved him
to be
made like unto his brethren
, that he might be a
merciful and faithful high priest
in things pertaining to God,
to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus.
Note:

Christ was made like unto His brethren so that He could understand the feelings of our infirmities. (See Hebrews 4:15) This qualified Him to be a merciful High Priest. Jesus suffered our temptations as a man so that in His heart He could feel and understand, and could make reconciliation for our sins. Jesus was the child of a human mother and therefore experienced temptations like all men. Yet He was without sin. Christ feels the feelings that we suffer and offers us His help and experience in our time of need.
13. What is the ultimate unknown latent sin that the final Day of Atonement cleanses?
Zechariah 12:10
And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications:
and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son, and shall be in bitterness for him, as one that is in bitterness for his firstborn.
Note:

Known sins required the death of the lamb in the sanctuary service. The Feast of Trumpets and the Day of Atonement were for unknown sins of both the individual and the nation. On the final Day of Atonement, Christ's High Priest ministry helps us to see the underlying cause as well as the act of our sins. When Adam and Eve sinned their nature became bent towards self. Sin then dwelt in their very nature. Mankind has a hard time seeing their own sin, so the Feast of Trumpets called on the people to examine their hearts and search out their hidden sinfulness.

Outward sins reveal inward brokenness. It is this broken part of humanity that Christ deals with in the final end-time atonement. Are we aware of the depth of our sin problem? Of course not! If we were aware, we would confess these sins and have them cleansed daily by the blood of the lamb.

Often sin lies latent in our hearts. Every individual sin that we commit, if drawn out to its final conclusion, desires the death of the Son of God. Latent within our hearts resides a secret; this secret lies below the surface. When we sin, our flesh wants to live, and we do not care that it will require the death of God’s dear son! Christ has not yet revealed the depth of this sin to His people in all of its awfulness. Only Jesus, our merciful high priest knows how to handle this delicate matter. When we finally see ourselves as God sees us, we will become brokenhearted. Thank God that He is merciful.
14. When Christ sprinkles our hearts from our evil conscience, What does He wash us with?
Hebrews 10:22
Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
Note:

This sprinkling is the final cleansing that takes place in humanity. As a people, we will then see how deeply sin resides in our heart. Unless this sin is revealed we will never be at-one-ment (atonement) with God. The entire price for sin was paid at the cross, but there still needs to be a final atonement for us to finally see what sin has done to us. When the sin of wanting the death of God is revealed, in mercy, Christ immediately ministers to us. He washed us with clean water so that we can truly be cleansed. (Christ is the living water. See John 7:38) When we see the depth of our sin, we will finally confess it and be cleansed. Then the atonement will become final.
15. What will be opened to us in that day?
Zechariah 13:1
In that day there shall be a fountain opened to the house of David and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem for sin and for uncleanness
2 And it shall come to pass in that day, saith the LORD of hosts, that
I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered: and also I will cause the prophets and the unclean spirit to pass out of the land.
Note:

We are washed with clean water on the final Day of Atonement. When God reveals the true hidden sin of His people, when we look upon the one whom we have pierced, we will then look upon ourselves as so filthy that it will take an entire fountain to cleanse us. But there is good news; this process will end all desire for sin in our hearts. The names of the idols will be cut out of the land, and they shall no more be remembered. (See verse two) Our conscience will become cleansed.
16. What was the feast day preceding the Day of Atonement?
Joel 2:14
Who knoweth if he will return and repent, and leave a blessing behind him; even a meat offering and a drink offering unto the LORD your God? 15
Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly.
Note:

Immediately preceding the Day of Atonement is the Feast of Trumpets. In Israel, the sound of the trumpet was an alarm call. It was a solemn assembly. It was a time of meditation, of self-scrutiny, of prayers, of hours spent in the synagogue to plead with God. It was a time to look at all of their wrongdoings and trespasses. A time to ask for forgiveness, to search one’s heart, to prepare for the Day of Atonement, and to look forward to becoming one with God.

Before God can cleanse our conscience on the antitypical Day of Atonement, our sins have to be confessed. The Feast of Trumpets helped Israel to understand the importance of searching their hearts and confessing the sins revealed there. Christ, in His High Priest ministry assists us in this work.
17. What happens to those who ignore the trumpet and fail to search their hearts and repent?
Zephaniah 1:4
I will also stretch out mine hand upon Judah, and upon all the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and
I will cut off the remnant of Baal from this place, and the name of the Chemarims with the priests;
And them that worship the host of heaven upon the housetops; and them that worship and that swear by the LORD, and that swear by Malcham;

And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil.
A day of the trumpet and alarm against the fenced cities,
and against the high towers.
Note:

The Chemarims were false priests who claimed to serve the Lord but at the same time they also swore by Malcham. Malcham was another name for Moloch / Baal. These priests were double-minded, they worshiped a combination of Baal and Jehovah. God says He will search Jerusalem (our hearts) with candles (strong flashlights) and punish them that are in the camps of both good and evil. This is a trumpet warning against those who neglect to search their hearts with meditation and scrutiny to prepare for the coming of the Lord.
The Chemarims were apostate priests. The word Chemarim comes from a root word that means “
black
”. These priests wore the white robes of Jehovah (See Leviticus 16:23) but their robes were blackened by tending to the fires of Baal. This is what it means when the Bible says; “
and thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Moloch
” (Leviticus 18:21).
We cannot be cleansed until we see the depths of the darkness that resides in the human heart. Adam did not know that his sin would affect the hearts of his descendants. “
The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it
?” (Jeremiah 17:9) Only as God’s cleansing fountain of clean water is opened will we be able to see the wickedness that resides latently in our hearts and be cleansed.

We can confidently say that we would have never allowed our children to pass through the fires to Moloch! But the underlying cause was idolatry. Our idolatry may have a different form but it exists as certainly as in those who committed this heinous act. When our sin is revealed, we can confess our sin and be cleansed! But not if we neglect to examine our hearts!
THE BLOTTING OUT OF OUR SINS:
18. How far does God remove our sins from us?
Psalm 103:12
As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us
Note:

It is at the end of time on the close of the antitypical Day of Atonement that Christ finally removes our sins from our conscience. Our sub-conscience is then cleansed and we will no longer remember our sins. He tells us that He will cast our sins into the bottom of the sea and that they will be no more! (See Micah 7:19) The final generation of God’s people will be cleansed from the effects of sin forever.
19. What must we do before our sins are blotted out?
Acts 3:19
Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out
, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord.
Note:

We must repent and be converted and then God will blot out our sins. When our sins are blotted out they are removed from us. Psalm 51:9 tells us that God will wash us, and we shall be whiter than snow.
20. What did David acknowledge before His sins were blotted out?
Psalm 51:1
Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness:
according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
2 Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin. 3
For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me
Note:
David had to acknowledge and repent of his sins before they could be blotted out. But David could not see his sins until Nathan the prophet pointed them out.
21. Whom alone did David say he sinned against?
Psalm 51:3
For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me. 4
Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight:
that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.
Note:
David had to examine himself to see the depth of his sin. When David finally saw himself, he exclaimed that his sin was “ever before him.” He then confessed that against God alone he had sinned.

We must have this experience if we desire to become cleansed. When we search our hearts we will be appalled by the sin we find there. We can then go to God in all humility confessing our guilt, He will then wash us and we shall be cleansed.

The time for this examination is not a future event. It is now that we are to begin this process. God does not reveal the depth of our transgressions all at once, He is too merciful for that. As many as he loves He rebukes and chastens: be zealous therefore, and repent. (See Revelation 3:19) To have our sins blotted out means that our sins no longer exist. At the end of time God’s people will be cleansed and their sins will be removed from their conscience. (See Hebrews 9:14)
22. What does God hide His face from when He blots out our iniquities?
Psalm 51: 9
Hide thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities.
Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
11 Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.
Note:
We cannot always see the depth of our sins. It is by examining our heart that we see ourselves as God sees us.
God cannot create a new heart in us until we first see and acknowledge our old heart. As we turn from our sins, He then renews a right spirit in us.
Psalm 51:10
Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
